key_insight: The paper shows that white-box probes can effectively detect AI deception and sabotage, even in frontier-style monitoring settings. By aggregating signals across many layers and tokens, the proposed probes achieve very strong detection performance, including 98.8% AUC on SHADE-Arena.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of monitoring LLM agents for hidden deception and sabotage, especially when harmful intent is not explicitly stated in the model’s output.
method: Collected the largest deception dataset to date for training white-box probes.
Introduced a novel probe architecture that aggregates information across many layers and tokens.
Evaluated the probes in frontier monitoring settings and compared them against a strong text-monitoring baseline.
impact: This matters because it offers a practical path for detecting deceptive model behavior before it causes harm. For AI practitioners, it strengthens the case for internal monitoring tools that can complement output-only safety checks.
visual_elements: Layered neural network diagram showing probe aggregation across tokens and layers

paper_title: Caught in the Act: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception
paper_authors: Oskar J. Hollinsworth, Alex F. Spies, Tigist Diriba, Adam Gleave, Chris Cundy
